newsitem.title: USA: U.S. businessman sues Air France over smoking charge.
newsitem.headline: U.S. businessman sues Air France over smoking charge.

text.p: A New York businessman is suing Air France, charging he was hauled partly naked from a passenger jet toilet seat by flight crew who suspected he was smoking, his attorney said on Wednesday.

Computer company owner Raviv Laor alleged in his $12 million lawsuit filed in Manhattan Supreme Court that he was abused and insulted by the crew and humiliated in front of other passengers on the flight from Paris to New York on May 19.
Officials from Air France were not immediately available for comment.

Laor, who is a U.S. citizen, said he was sitting in a locked bathroom on the non-smoking flight "with his pants and underpants down and in the process of going to the bathroom" when crew members smashed open the door and accused him of smoking after the smoke detector alarm went off.
"It turned out later the alarm was defective," Laor's attorney Michael Wolin said.

Laor, who says he is a non-smoker, charged that he was "viciously assaulted and physically attacked by several crew members who pulled him naked outside the bathroom exposing his genitals and other private body parts to seated passengers."
The lawyer said federal security regulations state a passenger must present an imminent and probable threat to the security of the plane for the crew to react in a responsible manner.
He said Laor, 27, presented no threat to the safety of the aircraft and that the crew had broken the law and violated Laor's rights.
